text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P0 model-serving errors across us-west-2. Elevated model load failures + GPU OOMs. Alert group: eng-runtime, eng-sre, support. See logs: https://logs.redwood/example/3319876543 :rotating_light:

sara (oncall): ack. I'm on it. spawning #incident-3319876543 now. @henry please triage runtime side, @maya check infra/GPU nodes, @alejandro collect customer impact.

henry (eng-runtime): looking at warmup logs from model-server-4: repeated deserialization failures then OOM at load. stack shows compile timeout then fallback attempt which triggers OOM. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:02Z] load_model(model_id=redwood/opt-6.7b-q8) -> deserialize error: EOF while reading
[2026-03-15T11:12:04Z] compile_kernels -> timeout (120s)
[2026-03-15T11:12:06Z] attempting fallback -> allocate GPU memory -> cudaError(2): out of memory
```

henry (eng-runtime): this looks like a combo: artifact truncated/deser + compile cache thrash causing memory pressure. multiple nodes in pool report high GPU alloc (~98%).

maya (sre): confirmed node flaps in us-west-2-gpupool-a. kube reports OOMKills on container runtime for model-warmup pods. node metrics: GPU mem free ~200MB, kernel crashes on nvml events.

alejandro (support): seeing customer tickets: 3 high-priority customers with 5xxs and tokenized rate spikes. Notifying account owners now. One customer on dedicated capacity reported request throttling then 503s since ~11:10 UTC.

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) prevent further warmups by disabling proactive warmup on affected pool, 2) scale up GPU pool by +2 nodes (hot add), 3) enable fallback to quantized variant (q4_0) for new loads, 4) temp route heavy customers to hosted fallback model. Which can we do fast?

henry (eng-runtime): can disable warmup via config flag for that nodepool in ~2m. Scaling +2 nodes depends on quota but I can trigger autoscale policy override. Fallback routing requires an immediate routing rule change in control plane - I can push a canary rule to map model family -> q4_0 variant for non-enterprise customers in ~5m.

maya (sre): I'll drain the worst node (gpu-12) to stop flapping containers and cordon it. Also starting a live nvml capture to ship with metrics.

henry (eng-runtime): quick playbook commands I'm running:
```bash
# disable proactive warmup for pool gpupool-a
redwoodctl pool update gpupool-a --warmup=false
# override autoscale to +2 nodes
redwoodctl pool scale gpupool-a --min 4 --max 10 --desired 6 --reason "incident 3319876543"
```

henry (eng-runtime): also applying a runtime hack: reduce compile threads from 8 -> 2 to lower peak memory during kernel compilation. patching config across pool.

alejandro (support): update: customers A and B confirmed degraded performance, customer C (enterprise) hit errors but they are on dedicated and unaffected? actually they reported intermittent 500s on some routes. I'm opening a direct bridge with AEs.

ryan (product-ops): tagging this as potential customer-impact P0. Do we need to enable rate-limiting / circuit-breaker on unstable routes to reduce load while we stabilize?

henry (eng-runtime): yes, enabling soft circuit-breaker: return 429 for > threshold to avoid warmup storms. Pushing route config now.

julia (eng-ml): quick note: the model artifacts were updated earlier today (new quantization artifact). If the artifact is corrupted it could cause deser EOF. Can someone check object-store checksums for the artifact? I have a previous good artifact hash.

henry (eng-runtime): i'll validate artifact hashes now against s3.

henry (eng-runtime): s3 check: artifact for redwood/opt-6.7b-q8 reported size 1.2GB but gzip header mismatch. Looks corrupted on region replicate. Pulling from older snapshot backup and starting a redeploy of that artifact to the pool.

maya (sre): node drain in progress. Replacing with node-28. Expected 90s to reattach GPU.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rolling redeploy started for model-server group 'warmup' (roll id r-331987). Links: https://ci.redwood/rolls/r-331987

henry (eng-runtime): redeploying older artifact plus lowered compile threads seems to let models load on node-28 in testing. Starting a small canary of 2 pods.

julia (eng-ml): if canary passes we should keep newer artifact out of rotation until we run full checksum/corpus eval. I'll prepare a checksum report + small eval on LLM-quality to ensure quantization matches.

alejandro (support): customers updated: A sees partial recovery on some endpoints, B still reporting 503s for high-throughput routes. Sending interim status email and asking for escalation if SLA breach imminent.

maya (sre): canary pods are green on node-28. nvml no errors after redeploy. rolling back cordon on other nodes after verifying.

henry (eng-runtime): canary verified on 2 pods. promoting rollback: disabling corrupted artifact and serving backup artifact. routing rule applied: new loads mapped to q4_0 variant until artifact is validated.

ryan (product-ops): good. please note in incident timeline: root cause appears to be corrupted artifact + compile-time memory spike causing cascading GPU OOMs and container crashes. Customer impact: transient 5xxs for some hosted and dedicated routes.

sara (oncall): summary of actions taken so far: - created incident channel #incident-3319876543 - disabled warmup on gpupool-a - drained and replaced flapping nodes - redeployed backup artifact - lowered compile threads - applied routing fallback to q4_0 for new loads - enabled soft circuit-breaker

sara (oncall): next steps: 1) followup checksum + origin diff (julia), 2) full postmortem if confirmed corrupted artifact (owner: henry), 3) customer outreach / SLA check (alejandro). I'll remain oncall until stable or handoff to next oncall at 13:00 UTC.

alejandro (support): opening incident status page and linking affected customers. I'll collect exact error samples and send to eng.
